prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1493; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and a neck strain. The account was taken by phone and the claimant said they were not represented by a lawyer.

Entry 2: The police report and two witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the impact. The other driver gave a statement that matches the claimant's account of how the collision happened.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show damage consistent with the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy. The claimant repeated the same account of events in every conversation so far, with no changes in the details.

Entry 5: The reported neck strain is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. The medical file shows a usual course of treatment that tapered off as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to the same area is known.

Entry 6: Based on the photos, witness statements, police report and medical records reviewed, the claim is progressing normally. Next steps are to confirm final treatment costs and close the injury portion once the claimant reports full recovery.
